To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GNM and ANN approaches applied to promolecular electron density networks are able to describe the collective dynamics of protein structures.

the GNM/ANM models are useful for the analysis of the collective motions of protein structures, and that the consideration of promolecular electron density distribution functions may provide a better description of the protein structure graph.

(1) the ED-based networks are more flexible than the Cα-based ones, (2) the flexibility of the ED-based networks is higher than that of Cα networks in the case of Crambin, and (3) the ED-based network flexibility is lower than that of the Cα network for Pancreatic Trysin Inhibitor (PTI).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for calculating the electron density distribution function (ED) of a macromolecule from the X-ray structure.
the study of the collective motions of protein structures from the smoothed electron density (ED).
the application of the network model approach to the study of the collective motions of protein structure graphs obtained from calculated promolecular ED distribution functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GNM/ANM approaches applied to protein ED distributions are useful tools to describe collective motions in proteins.
the use of promolecular ED distributions for the calculation of protein dynamics may lead to a better understanding of the role of crystal packing and of the side chains.
the GNM/ANM approaches applied to protein structure graphs built with promolecular ED distributions are a powerful and useful tool for the analysis of protein dynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GNM and the ANM approaches are able to reproduce the collective motions of protein structures built from smoothed ED distributions.
the use of promolecular ED distribution functions for the construction of protein structure graphs is an effective tool to describe protein dynamics at the atomic level.

we have shown the possibility to describe the collective motions of proteins by using the Gaussian Network Model and the Anisotropic Network model approaches applied to networks built from promolecular electron density distributions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GNM and ANN approaches can be successfully applied to protein structure graphs built with promolecular electron density distributions.
the ED-based approach can be a useful tool in the study of protein dynamics.
the ED network approach can provide a better description of the dynamics of proteins.
